correctness.rationale: For synchronous OR, the relevant support comes from exact-length walks, not automatically from distance balls. Johnson distance is k−|A∩B|; replacing an edge by a two-edge path around a triangle, then inserting backtracks as needed, reaches either parity at all lengths at least the positive distance. Closed walks of lengths 2 and 3 handle distance zero for times ≥2. Thus at t=k−r the zero sites are exactly the k-cliques of uncovered r-faces. For a fixed tuple of h distinct sites, its e distinct faces have e·m_n+O(n^(k−r−1)) forbidden seed blocks by the union bound and the pairwise containment-family inclusion–exclusion bound. For fixed h the Bernoulli vacancy probability is uniformly n^(−ke/b)exp(−ce)(1+o(1)), since p²m_n and the overlap correction multiplied by p vanish. An overlap type on v labels has O(n^v) copies. Within each connected component of the site intersection graph, order the sites by a connected traversal. A new site with s labels already seen adds k−s labels and at least b−binom(s,r) faces, so the exponent v−ke/b changes by at most −s+(k/b)binom(s,r), strictly negative when 1≤s<k for r≥2 and nonpositive for s=k. The second site in a nonsingleton component is distinct and enforces strict negativity. Disjoint tuples alone contribute (exp(−bc)/k!)^h, giving Poisson convergence by factorial moments. By absorption of the all-ones state, earlier consensus would require a fixed site to be active at t−1, bounded by O(log n/n) from its candidate seed blocks even when t−1=1. Complete (r−1)-coverage follows by a union bound with vacancy exp(−Θ(n log n)); full r-coverage fails with high probability by a diverging mean and uniform pair-probability factor 1+o(1). At r=1, the uncovered-label Poisson law and the identity Y=binom(X,k) give a lower tail, not a Poisson zero count at the site level. All nonempty states fill by k and a singleton seed has a disjoint site not reached earlier. The two frozen scripts were inspected, not run. The nominal 26,180 figure counts update iterations, including time one where no ball assertion is made; the asymptotic proof does not use these diagnostics.

evidence: Cooley–Kang–Koch count j-sets of a fixed degree and obtain the Poisson isolation limit at leading coefficient j. Riordan couples clique hypergraphs of binomial hosts to independent hypergraphs one-sidedly for factor thresholds; that is not a coupling for the vacancies of faces in a denser covering shadow.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither general deterministic OR transient machinery, extremal Johnson domination, independent-host clique counting, nor the high-order connectivity hitting-time theorem subsumes the dependent vacant-clique law in the stated parameter window. The triangle detours and strictly balanced exponent calculation are what give the indicated consensus times.

evidence: For j=r and degree zero, CKK's Poisson window has p=(r log n+c_n)/m_n with c_n=o(log n). Matching the proposed p would need c_n=(k/b−r)log n+c, outside that hypothesis. The number of isolated r-faces here has mean of order n^(r−k/b)→∞. The same CKK theorem at j=1 does supply the earlier-known isolated-label law used in the contextual endpoint.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The proof of the frozen law is not obtained by putting j=r in the known theorem. One needs simultaneous vacancy on all b faces of a candidate block and must suppress overlapping candidate clusters. At r=1, by contrast, the consensus lower tail is a short consequence of the known isolated-label limit and the distance equivalence; it is not independent evidence of originality.

One must control these overlaps to transport the independent strict-balance intuition.

originality.rationale: The original part is the sequence of interior vacancy-clique thresholds and their precise two-time consensus law. Ordinary Johnson geometry, general OR-network propagation tools and the r=1 uncovered-label Poisson law do not themselves constitute novel contributions. The earlier full-coverage results count a different obstruction at a strictly later scale; the usual independent-edge clique theorem does not apply to this dependent shadow without the additional joint vacancy argument.
residual_risks: Godbole–Janson full text was inaccessible in lawful attempts; its exact theorem and possible ancillary statements were not independently verified.

value.rationale: The exact-length network reduction poses a natural random coverage question that full coverage does not answer. For every intermediate update the theorem identifies a distinct scale and a sharp nondegenerate probability profile while showing that many faces remain uncovered. The failure of the same clique-count Poisson mechanism at the first-shadow boundary explains why the final pair of times has a different probability law. This is useful beyond a deterministic diameter bound or a first-moment threshold estimate, within the fixed-k scope.
